statement: The aggregation floor — the gap between the instantaneous coefficient and the Delta-window mean of it, before any estimator is fitted — is -2.63% to -1.23% across the four alpha channels at annual reporting and -0.22% to -0.11% at monthly. It is exactly proportional to Delta: floor/Delta varies by at most 0.00057 nats/yr across Delta = 1/12 to 1 yr, against channel values of 0.0127-0.0261 nats/yr, which is the first-order prediction floor = -(Delta/2) dlog(alpha)/dt confirmed numerically.
On the log-log scale the floor grows with Delta at slope +0.998 [+0.994, +1.005], against the analytic prediction of +1.

UDE (continuous, mixed operator): the slope of |bias| on log N, holding the aggregation interval and the channel fixed, is +0.0009 nats per e-fold [-0.0087, +0.0049] over N = 11 to 469 — no detectable N dependence. Over the whole measured range that bounds any change in bias at 1.8 percentage points.

per-flow AR/ARX (discrete, on totals): the slope of |bias| on log N, holding the aggregation interval and the channel fixed, is +0.0078 nats per e-fold [-0.0460, +0.0815] over N = 11 to 469 — no detectable N dependence. Over the whole measured range that bounds any change in bias at 30.6 percentage points.

Directly rather than through a slope: of the 24 (class, Delta, channel) cells, 2 swing across N by more than the eight-draw replicate spread of the same class and channel, and the swings are non-monotone in N in 7 of 24. More data moves the bias around; it does not move it towards zero.

UDE (continuous, mixed operator): scored against both candidate estimands, it is closer to the Delta-window aggregate than to the instantaneous coefficient in 41 of 84 (arm, channel) cells at Delta <= 1 yr (two-sided binomial p = 0.9132); median |bias| 1.07% against the point value and 1.12% against the window mean, with a floor of 1.39%.

per-flow AR/ARX (discrete, on totals): scored against both candidate estimands, it is closer to the Delta-window aggregate than to the instantaneous coefficient in 58 of 84 (arm, channel) cells at Delta <= 1 yr (two-sided binomial p = 0.0006); median |bias| 1.55% against the point value and 0.89% against the window mean, with a floor of 1.39%.

UDE (continuous, mixed operator): the pass-through of the aggregation floor into the reported coefficient is b = +0.580 [+0.514, +0.834] (b = 1 inherits the whole floor, b = 0 escapes it) — partial pass-through, and neither 0 nor 1.

per-flow AR/ARX (discrete, on totals): the pass-through of the aggregation floor into the reported coefficient is b = +0.186 [+0.038, +0.838] (b = 1 inherits the whole floor, b = 0 escapes it) — partial pass-through, and neither 0 nor 1.

UDE (continuous, mixed operator) on the noise-free annual record, where the only bias available is the aggregation one: cc -0.16% (floor -1.23%), dr -1.42% (floor -1.54%), refc -0.36% (floor -2.63%), win -2.92% (floor -1.85%).

per-flow AR/ARX (discrete, on totals) on the noise-free annual record, where the only bias available is the aggregation one: cc -1.38% (floor -1.23%), dr -2.76% (floor -1.54%), refc -1.48% (floor -2.63%), win -3.91% (floor -1.85%).

UDE (continuous, mixed operator): across eight independent noise draws of the same annual record — same truth, same Delta, same N — the bias moves over 2.33–6.73 percentage points. Nothing smaller than that is reported as a finding anywhere in this package.

per-flow AR/ARX (discrete, on totals): across eight independent noise draws of the same annual record — same truth, same Delta, same N — the bias moves over 1.89–9.98 percentage points. Nothing smaller than that is reported as a finding anywhere in this package.

On the `season` twin, whose alpha_refc carries four sub-annual components (two at exact annual harmonics), the floor does not fall in proportion to Delta the way it does on the smooth twin: 1 yr -8.2%, 0.5 yr -17.4%, 1/4 yr -14.2%, 1 mo -4.2%. The first-order law holds only while Delta is short against the period of the fastest component.

Splitting that floor by mechanism: the two components at exact annual harmonics carry -9.75% of systematic offset with 6.1 pp of dispersion, the two non-harmonic components -1.49% of offset with 14.9 pp of dispersion. The harmonic figure agrees with its closed form to 0.11 pp. This is WP-11f's transfer-function result reached from the estimand side: annual reporting turns a harmonic sub-annual component into a constant, invisible offset and a non-harmonic one into dispersion.
UDE (continuous, mixed operator) on that channel: 1 yr -11.4%, 0.5 yr -9.0%, 1/4 yr -9.9%, 1 mo -10.4% — finer observation does not remove it.
per-flow AR/ARX (discrete, on totals) on that channel: 1 yr -12.3%, 0.5 yr -8.2%, 1/4 yr -10.6%, 1 mo -7.7% — finer observation does not remove it.
